verdict.rationale: Auth0's first-party AI docs say agents can use CIBA to request user approval for sensitive operations via push notifications, SMS, or email, even when the user is not actively using the app. The docs present this as human-in-the-loop control for AI agents, and Strong Customer Authentication with Dynamic Linking ties approval to transaction details. missing for 10: in-depth implementation documentation (approval request lifecycle, polling/timeouts, agent SDK integration specifics), independent or hands-on corroboration that the CIBA agent approval flow works as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require asynchronous human approval (e.g. CIBA-style confirmation) before an autonomous agent completes a sensitive transaction

citations.quote: Using standards like CIBA (Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication), agents can request approval for sensitive operations via push notifications, SMS, or email, even when the user is not actively using the application.
Secure your AI agents with user authentication, delegated authorization, human-in-the-loop controls with CIBA, and fine-grained authorization in RAG pipelines.
Dynamic Linking ties transaction details to the SCA approval confirmation to help prevent transaction tampering.
